authority.name: Clay Mathematics Institute
authority.problem_title: Existence and Smoothness of the Navier-Stokes Equation
authority.author: Charles L. Fefferman

equations: partial_t u + (u dot grad)u = nu Delta u - grad p + f

official_formulations.initial_data: any smooth divergence-free rapidly decaying u0 satisfying Fefferman condition (4)
official_formulations.required_conclusion: global smooth p,u on R^3 x [0,infinity) satisfying the equations and bounded energy

official_formulations.initial_data: any smooth divergence-free spatially periodic u0 satisfying Fefferman condition (8)
official_formulations.required_conclusion: global smooth spatially periodic p,u on R^3 x [0,infinity)

official_formulations.initial_data: there exists smooth divergence-free rapidly decaying u0 satisfying Fefferman condition (4)
official_formulations.forcing: there exists smooth rapidly decaying f satisfying Fefferman condition (5)
official_formulations.required_conclusion: no global physically reasonable solution p,u satisfying the equations, global smoothness, and bounded energy

official_formulations.initial_data: there exists smooth divergence-free spatially periodic u0 satisfying Fefferman condition (8)
official_formulations.forcing: there exists smooth spatially periodic f with time decay satisfying Fefferman condition (9)
official_formulations.required_conclusion: no global smooth spatially periodic solution p,u satisfying the equations

errata.statement: The pressure periodicity condition p(x+e_j,t)=p(x,t) must be made explicit in the periodic assumptions.
Fefferman's PDF includes a corrected weak-form equation in the errata; use the erratum rather than silently reproducing the earlier printed form.
